messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Multiple QTL model analysis with covariate
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Multiple QTL model analysis with covariate
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

Now that I have performed the stepwiseQTL analysis, I get some contradictory results.

So in the scanone, I don't find significant QTLs. In the scantwo, i find some pairs of interacting QTLs, that have LODs that are slightly higher than the significance tresholds.  I combined these QTLs in a Multiple QTL model and then used refineQTL and fitQTL to get the results for the complete model.
Here I get several QTLs that are clearly over the significance threshold, so that are clearly significant.
Strangely when I then do the stepwiseQTL, no significant QTLs model comes out at all.

See below the results from the refineQTL & fitQTL, and the significance threshold (from scantwo permutation test with method="em"). (I had to mask the positions of the QTLs with letters due to the confidentiality of my PhD project)

Which result should I trust now, the results from the stepwiseQTL, or from the refineQTL & fitQTL? Also, what I dont completely understand yet, how do the LOD-scores from this multiple QTL model compare to the LOD-scores from the simple scanone analysis? As with scanone I dont get any really significant peaks? How can there be such differences between the different methods?

Thanks!

Best Wishes,
Jasper

Perm (1008 permutations)
    full  fv1  int  add  av1  one
20% 5.33 4.21 3.28 4.15 2.85 2.16
5%  6.10 4.78 3.90 4.89 3.38 2.76
1%  6.78 5.33 4.46 5.52 4.00 3.47

Full model result
----------------------------------
Model formula: y ~ Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4 + Q5 + Q6 + Q1:Q2 + Q3:Q4

       df       SS        MS      LOD     %var Pvalue(Chi2)    Pvalue(F)
Model   8 10948.65 1368.5808 16.56774 31.45702 2.711165e-13 7.853718e-13
Error 193 23856.45  123.6086
Total 201 34805.10

Drop one QTL at a time ANOVA table:

This seems rather extreme in my opinion. I was expecting to have ~1000 markers remaining. Is there a possibility of something else going wrong besides having poor marker data/identical markers? I will also note that some markers are SNPs and others are indels as well.

my code is as follows:
print(dup<-findDupMarkers(map, exact.only=FALSE))
#the above lists over 7000 markers that are exact

I am attaching a "dummy.version" of my file for you as well.

Best,
Sarah

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Genetic Mapping: Deleting Duplicate Markers
messages.body_plain:
There do seem to be a large number of effectively duplicate markers, but when I drop the duplicates, I still have 1841 markers left.

  library(qtl)
  x <- read.cross("csv", file="dummy.map.csv", genotypes=c("A", "B"), crosstype="riself")
  dup <- findDupMarkers(x, exact.only=FALSE)
  length(dup)           # 1001 groups of duplicated markers
  length( unlist(dup) ) # 5727 markers that you might drop

  x_reduced <- drop.markers(x, unlist(dup) )

  totmar(x)         # 7568 markers
  totmar(x_reduced) # 1841 markers (= 7568 - 5727)

You could pull out the genotype data and look at a set of these duplicates.

  g <- pull.geno(x)
  g_dup1 <- g[, c(names(dup)[1], dup[[1]])]
  dim(g_dup1) # 65 lines x 32 markers
  g_dup1

They do look all the same, though with some having a lot of missing genotypes.

karl

Hi Karl,

Thank you for the advice so far. Unfortunately after running your code I did not get remotely similar results. When running your code my object dup had 26 markers and the length of the unlisted object dup was 7540. Before identifying duplicate markers, I run the loop in your genetic mapping article for removing duplicate individuals. Before eliminating the duplicate markers the map file has 7566 markers.

#running loop eliminating mismatching genotypes
for(i in 1:nrow(wh)) {
  tozero<-!is.na <http://is.na>(g[wh[i,1],]) & !is.na <http://is.na>(g[wh[i,2],]) &
    g[wh[i,1],] != g[wh[i,2],]
  map$geno[[1]]$data[wh[i,1],tozero]<-NA
}

#omit one individual for each pair
map<-subset(map, ind = wh[,2])
totmar(map) #returns value of 7566

#looking for duplicate markers
dup<-findDupMarkers(map, exact.only = F)
length(dup) #returns value of 26
length(unlist(dup)) #returns value of 7540

Earlier on I also do more quality control of eliminating Individuals missing many markers and markers missing genotypes. But if through that I narrow my markers down to 7566 markers, I don't see how it still narrows down to 26 markers that aren't duplicates?

Thanks,
Sarah

messages.body_plain:
At this step in your script:

   map<-subset(map, ind = wh[,2])

you are omitting all but 5 of the individuals

That's the reason that at the next step, the markers look to be largely
duplicates; there are just five individuals left.

I don't think there is overwhelming evidence for duplicate samples, and
so I wouldn't omit any samples. The closest pair has 7% mismatch.

karl

The error is saying it’s trying to create an object that is larger than the largest allowed object. It’s not feasible, with R/qtl, to do scantwo() with such a large number of markers.

R/qtl has no code to take advantage of GPUs.

karl

messages.subject: plot.scanone error?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Karl,

I'm analyzing BC1 data and am having an issue with the analysis of the X chromosome. All individuals are males. Below are my cross object and genetic map.

> mapthis3
  This is an object of class "cross".
  It is too complex to print, so we provide just this summary.
    Backcross

    No. individuals:    808

    No. phenotypes:     3
    Percent phenotyped: 100 100 100

    No. chromosomes:    3
        Autosomes:      2 3
        X chr:          X

    Total markers:      860
    No. markers:        440 392 28
    Percent genotyped:  97.9
    Genotypes (%):
          Autosomes:    AA:24.3  AB:75.7
       X chromosome:    AY:71.5  BY:28.5

> summaryMap(mapthis3)
        n.mar length ave.spacing max.spacing
2         440  199.7         0.5        11.0
3         392   99.2         0.3         4.6
X          28    3.7         0.1         0.4
overall   860  302.6         0.4        11.0

As you can see the length of the X is very small (3.7 cM) due to an inversion that suppresses X chromosome recombination. However, when I scan for QTL, the length of this chromosome is expanded in the results.

> mapthis3 <- calc.genoprob(mapthis3, step=0, map.function = c("kosambi"), off.end=0, error.prob=0.0001)
> mapthis3 <- calc.errorlod(mapthis3, error.prob=0.0001, map.function="kosambi", version="new")
> out.hk <http://out.hk> <- scanone (mapthis3, pheno.col=c(1), method="hk")
> summary(out.hk <http://out.hk>)
            chr  pos    lod
2:R45780390   2 97.9   4.19
c3.loc38      3 43.0  17.83
X:4620940     X 11.2 215.32

The QTL on the X is at position 11.3 cM. Do you have an idea of what could be causing this? When I plot the X the map is the appropriate length, but starts at 10 cM (see the attached plot).

Thank you,

Kevin

messages.subject: Re: plot.scanone error?
messages.body_plain:
After some trial and error I found that his problem seems to have been caused by the "exact.only=TRUE" option in findDupMarkers upstream of the genetic map calculation.

These commands result in the error:

findDupMarkers(mapthis3, exact.only=TRUE, adjacent.only=TRUE)
mapthis3 <- drop.markers(mapthis3, unlist(dupmar.adjonly))

These do not:

dupmar.adjonly <- findDupMarkers(mapthis, adjacent.only=TRUE)
mapthis3 <- drop.markers(mapthis3, unlist(dupmar.adjonly))

Best,

Kevin
